def add_rule(doc):
    p=doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(6)
    r=p.add_run('─'*108)
    r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(LIGHT_BLUE); r.font.size=Pt(5)


def add_bullet(doc, text, level=0, bold_prefix=None):
    p=doc.add_paragraph(style='Normal')
    p.paragraph_format.left_indent=Inches(0.22+0.18*level)
    p.paragraph_format.first_line_indent=Inches(-0.15)
    p.add_run('• ').bold=True
    if bold_prefix and text.startswith(bold_prefix):
        p.add_run(bold_prefix).bold=True; p.add_run(text[len(bold_prefix):])
    else: p.add_run(text)
    return p


def add_redline_para(doc, label, deleted=None, added=None, note=None):
    p=doc.add_paragraph(style='Redline')
    p.paragraph_format.left_indent=Inches(0.15)
    rr=p.add_run(label + ' '); rr.bold=True; rr.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(BLUE)
    if deleted:
        d=p.add_run(deleted); d.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(RED); d.font.strike=True
    if deleted and added:
        sep=p.add_run('  →  '); sep.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(GRAY)
    if added:
        a=p.add_run(added); a.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(RED); a.font.underline=True
    if note:
        n=p.add_run('  ' + note); n.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(GRAY); n.font.italic=True
    return p


def add_current(doc, text):
    p=doc.add_paragraph(style='Small Text')
    p.paragraph_format.left_indent=Inches(0.15)
    r=p.add_run('Draft: '); r.bold=True; r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(GRAY)
    p.add_run(text)
    return p


def add_comment_callout(doc, code, priority, position, basis, risk, comment_id=None, anchor=None):
    table=doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=1)
    table.alignment=WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    cell=table.cell(0,0); cell.vertical_alignment=WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    fill = LIGHT_RED if priority=='Critical' else LIGHT_YELLOW if priority=='Significant' else LIGHT_BLUE
    set_cell_shading(cell, fill); set_cell_margins(cell, 100, 130, 100, 130)
    set_cell_border(cell, top={'val':'single','sz':'6','color':'A6A6A6'}, bottom={'val':'single','sz':'6','color':'A6A6A6'}, left={'val':'single','sz':'12','color':RED if priority=='Critical' else BLUE}, right={'val':'single','sz':'6','color':'A6A6A6'})
    p=cell.paragraphs[0]; p.style='Callout'; p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(2)
    r=p.add_run(f'Comment {code} — {priority} — {position}'); r.bold=True; r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(RED if priority=='Critical' else BLUE)
    for label, val in [('Basis', basis), ('Risk', risk)]:
        pp=cell.add_paragraph(style='Callout'); pp.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(1)
        rr=pp.add_run(label + ': '); rr.bold=True
        pp.add_run(val)
    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(1)
    return table


def add_issue(doc, code, priority, section, title, current, deleted, added, position, basis, risk, extra=None):
    p=doc.add_paragraph(style='Heading 2')
    r=p.add_run(f'{code}  |  {priority.upper()}  |  {section} — {title}')
    keep_with_next(p)
    comment_text=f'{priority} / {position}. Basis: {basis} Risk: {risk}'
    c=doc.comments.add_comment(comment_text, author='Polaris Seller\'s Counsel', initials='PSC')
    r.mark_comment_range(r, c.comment_id)
    add_current(doc, current)
    add_redline_para(doc, 'DELETE', deleted=deleted)
    add_redline_para(doc, 'ADD', added=added)
    add_comment_callout(doc, code, priority, position, basis, risk)
    if extra:
        p=doc.add_paragraph(style='Small Text'); p.add_run(extra)
    return p


def add_table(doc, headers, rows, widths=None, font=8.2):
    table=doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers))
    table.alignment=WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    table.style='Table Grid'
    hdr=table.rows[0]; set_repeat_table_header(hdr)
    for i,h in enumerate(headers):
        c=hdr.cells[i]; set_cell_shading(c, NAVY); set_cell_margins(c, 90, 90, 90, 90); c.vertical_alignment=WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
        p=c.paragraphs[0]; p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(0); p.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
        r=p.add_run(h); r.bold=True; r.font.name='Arial'; r.font.size=Pt(font); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(255,255,255)
    for ridx,row in enumerate(rows):
        cells=table.add_row().cells
        for i,val in enumerate(row):
            c=cells[i]; set_cell_margins(c, 80, 90, 80, 90); c.vertical_alignment=WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT.TOP
            if ridx%2==1: set_cell_shading(c, LIGHT_GRAY)
            p=c.paragraphs[0]; p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(0)
            r=p.add_run(str(val)); r.font.name='Arial'; r.font.size=Pt(font)
    if widths:
        for row in table.rows:
            for i,w in enumerate(widths): row.cells[i].width=Inches(w)
    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(1)
    return table


def add_section_heading(doc, text, level=1):
    p=doc.add_paragraph(text, style=f'Heading {level}')
    keep_with_next(p)
    return p

block.text:
**Considering responsibilities for compliance**

I need to think about Trident, as the owner/operator after Closing, and their primary responsibilities. They’ll need to maintain or obtain certification and manage reports and records. Compliance with customs and trade regulations seems really important here, too. Plus, I should remember the costs associated with these responsibilities. There’s a lot to unpack, and I want to ensure all requirements are clear for them to manage effectively!

{"command":"python - <<'PY'
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Inches, Pt, RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH, WD_BREAK
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT, WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT
from docx.enum.section import WD_SECTION
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.enum.style import WD_STYLE_TYPE
from docx.enum.text import WD_LINE_SPACING
from docx.enum.section import WD_ORIENT
from docx.enum.table import WD_ROW_HEIGHT_RULE
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime

OUT = Path('output')
OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

NAVY = '17365D'
BLUE = '1F4E79'
RED = 'C00000'
GREEN = '008000'
GRAY = '666666'
LIGHT_BLUE = 'D9EAF7'
LIGHT_GRAY = 'F2F2F2'
LIGHT_YELLOW = 'FFF2CC'
LIGHT_RED = 'FCE4D6'
LIGHT_GREEN = 'E2F0D9'


def set_cell_shading(cell, fill):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = tcPr.find(qn('w:shd'))
    if shd is None:
        shd = OxmlElement('w:shd')
        tcPr.append(shd)
    shd.set(qn('w:fill'), fill)


def set_cell_margins(cell, top=80, start=100, bottom=80, end=100):
    tc = cell._tc
    tcPr = tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    tcMar = tcPr.first_child_found_in('w:tcMar')
    if tcMar is None:
        tcMar = OxmlElement('w:tcMar')
        tcPr.append(tcMar)
    for m, v in [('top', top), ('start', start), ('bottom', bottom), ('end', end)]:
        node = tcMar.find(qn(f'w:{m}'))
        if node is None:
            node = OxmlElement(f'w:{m}')
            tcMar.append(node)
        node.set(qn('w:w'), str(v))
        node.set(qn('w:type'), 'dxa')


def set_cell_border(cell, **kwargs):
    tc = cell._tc
    tcPr = tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    tcBorders = tcPr.first_child_found_in('w:tcBorders')
    if tcBorders is None:
        tcBorders = OxmlElement('w:tcBorders')
        tcPr.append(tcBorders)
    for edge in ('top', 'left', 'bottom', 'right', 'insideH', 'insideV'):
        if edge in kwargs:
            tag = 'w:{}'.format(edge)
            element = tcBorders.find(qn(tag))
            if element is None:
                element = OxmlElement(tag)
                tcBorders.append(element)
            for key in ['val','sz','space','color']:
                if key in kwargs[edge]:
                    element.set(qn('w:{}'.format(key)), str(kwargs[edge][key]))


def set_repeat_table_header(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    tblHeader = OxmlElement('w:tblHeader')
    tblHeader.set(qn('w:val'), 'true')
    trPr.append(tblHeader)


def keep_with_next(p):
    pPr = p._p.get_or_add_pPr()
    k = OxmlElement('w:keepNext')
    pPr.append(k)


def set_keep_together(p):
    pPr = p._p.get_or_add_pPr()
    k = OxmlElement('w:keepLines')
    pPr.append(k)


def add_page_number(paragraph):
    run = paragraph.add_run()
    fldChar1 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); fldChar1.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'begin')
    instrText = OxmlElement('w:instrText'); instrText.set(qn('xml:space'), 'preserve'); instrText.text = 'PAGE'
    fldChar2 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); fldChar2.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'end')
    run._r.append(fldChar1); run._r.append(instrText); run._r.append(fldChar2)


def setup(doc, title, short_title):
    sec = doc.sections[0]
    sec.top_margin = Inches(0.7)
    sec.bottom_margin = Inches(0.7)
    sec.left_margin = Inches(0.8)
    sec.right_margin = Inches(0.8)
    sec.header_distance = Inches(0.3)
    sec.footer_distance = Inches(0.35)
    styles = doc.styles
    styles['Normal'].font.name = 'Arial'; styles['Normal']._element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn('w:eastAsia'), 'Arial'); styles['Normal'].font.size = Pt(9.2)
    styles['Normal'].paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
    styles['Normal'].paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.05
    for sname, size, color in [('Title', 20, NAVY), ('Heading 1', 14, NAVY), ('Heading 2', 11.5, BLUE), ('Heading 3', 10, BLUE)]:
        st = styles[sname]
        st.font.name = 'Arial'; st._element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn('w:eastAsia'), 'Arial'); st.font.size = Pt(size); st.font.bold = True; st.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(color)
        st.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(8); st.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
    for name in ['Redline', 'Callout', 'Small Text', 'Table Text']:
        if name not in styles:
            st = styles.add_style(name, WD_STYLE_TYPE.PARAGRAPH)
        else: st = styles[name]
        st.font.name = 'Arial'; st._element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn('w:eastAsia'), 'Arial')
    styles['Redline'].font.size = Pt(9)
    styles['Redline'].paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
    styles['Callout'].font.size = Pt(8.7)
    styles['Small Text'].font.size = Pt(8)
    styles['Small Text'].font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(GRAY)
    styles['Table Text'].font.size = Pt(8.2)
    # Header/footer
    header = sec.header.paragraphs[0]
    header.text = short_title
    header.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.RIGHT
    for r in header.runs:
        r.font.name = 'Arial'; r.font.size = Pt(8); r.font.italic = True; r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(GRAY)
    footer = sec.footer.paragraphs[0]
    footer.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    r = footer.add_run('PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY-CLIENT WORK PRODUCT   |   ')
    r.font.name = 'Arial'; r.font.size = Pt(8); r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(GRAY)
    r2 = footer.add_run('Page '); r2.font.name='Arial'; r2.font.size=Pt(8); r2.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(GRAY)
    add_page_number(footer)
    # core props
    doc.core_properties.title = title
    doc.core_properties.subject = 'Seller-side review of Trident draft TSA'
    doc.core_properties.author = 'Whitfield & Crane LLP'
    doc.core_properties.comments = 'Prepared for Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc.'


def add_title_block(doc, title, subtitle, date='May 9, 2025'):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    r = p.add_run('PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL\n')
    r.bold=True; r.font.size=Pt(9); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(RED)
    r2 = p.add_run('ATTORNEY-CLIENT WORK PRODUCT')
    r2.bold=True; r2.font.size=Pt(9); r2.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(RED)
    p2 = doc.add_paragraph(style='Title'); p2.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER; p2.add_run(title)
    p3 = doc.add_paragraph(); p3.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    rr=p3.add_run(subtitle); rr.font.size=Pt(10); rr.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(GRAY)
    p4=doc.add_paragraph(); p4.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    rd=p4.add_run(date); rd.font.size=Pt(9); rd.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(GRAY)
    p5=doc.add_paragraph(); p5.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    rr=p5.add_run('Prepared for Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc.'); rr.bold=True; rr.font.size=Pt(9)


def add_rule(doc):
    p=doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(6)
    r=p.add_run('─'*108)
    r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(LIGHT_BLUE); r.font.size=Pt(5)


def add_bullet(doc, text, level=0, bold_prefix=None):
    p=doc.add_paragraph(style='Normal')
    p.paragraph_format.left_indent=Inches(0.22+0.18*level)
    p.paragraph_format.first_line_indent=Inches(-0.15)
    p.add_run('• ').bold=True
    if bold_prefix and text.startswith(bold_prefix):
        p.add_run(bold_prefix).bold=True; p.add_run(text[len(bold_prefix):])
    else: p.add_run(text)
    return p


def add_redline_para(doc, label, deleted=None, added=None, note=None):
    p=doc.add_paragraph(style='Redline')
    p.paragraph_format.left_indent=Inches(0.15)
    rr=p.add_run(label + ' '); rr.bold=True; rr.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(BLUE)
    if deleted:
        d=p.add_run(deleted); d.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(RED); d.font.strike=True
    if deleted and added:
        sep=p.add_run('  →  '); sep.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(GRAY)
    if added:
        a=p.add_run(added); a.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(RED); a.font.underline=True
    if note:
        n=p.add_run('  ' + note); n.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(GRAY); n.font.italic=True
    return p


def add_current(doc, text):
    p=doc.add_paragraph(style='Small Text')
    p.paragraph_format.left_indent=Inches(0.15)
    r=p.add_run('Draft: '); r.bold=True; r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(GRAY)
    p.add_run(text)
    return p


def add_comment_callout(doc, code, priority, position, basis, risk, comment_id=None, anchor=None):
    table=doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=1)
    table.alignment=WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    cell=table.cell(0,0); cell.vertical_alignment=WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    fill = LIGHT_RED if priority=='Critical' else LIGHT_YELLOW if priority=='Significant' else LIGHT_BLUE
    set_cell_shading(cell, fill); set_cell_margins(cell, 100, 130, 100, 130)
    set_cell_border(cell, top={'val':'single','sz':'6','color':'A6A6A6'}, bottom={'val':'single','sz':'6','color':'A6A6A6'}, left={'val':'single','sz':'12','color':RED if priority=='Critical' else BLUE}, right={'val':'single','sz':'6','color':'A6A6A6'})
    p=cell.paragraphs[0]; p.style='Callout'; p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(2)
    r=p.add_run(f'Comment {code} — {priority} — {position}'); r.bold=True; r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(RED if priority=='Critical' else BLUE)
    for label, val in [('Basis', basis), ('Risk', risk)]:
        pp=cell.add_paragraph(style='Callout'); pp.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(1)
        rr=pp.add_run(label + ': '); rr.bold=True
        pp.add_run(val)
    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(1)
    return table


def add_issue(doc, code, priority, section, title, current, deleted, added, position, basis, risk, extra=None):
    p=doc.add_paragraph(style='Heading 2')
    r=p.add_run(f'{code}  |  {priority.upper()}  |  {section} — {title}')
    keep_with_next(p)
    comment_text=f'{priority} / {position}. Basis: {basis} Risk: {risk}'
    c=doc.comments.add_comment(comment_text, author='Polaris Seller\'s Counsel', initials='PSC')
    r.mark_comment_range(r, c.comment_id)
    add_current(doc, current)
    add_redline_para(doc, 'DELETE', deleted=deleted)
    add_redline_para(doc, 'ADD', added=added)
    add_comment_callout(doc, code, priority, position, basis, risk)
    if extra:
        p=doc.add_paragraph(style='Small Text'); p.add_run(extra)
    return p


def add_table(doc, headers, rows, widths=None, font=8.2):
    table=doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers))
    table.alignment=WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    table.style='Table Grid'
    hdr=table.rows[0]; set_repeat_table_header(hdr)
    for i,h in enumerate(headers):
        c=hdr.cells[i]; set_cell_shading(c, NAVY); set_cell_margins(c, 90, 90, 90, 90); c.vertical_alignment=WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
        p=c.paragraphs[0]; p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(0); p.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
        r=p.add_run(h); r.bold=True; r.font.name='Arial'; r.font.size=Pt(font); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(255,255,255)
    for ridx,row in enumerate(rows):
        cells=table.add_row().cells
        for i,val in enumerate(row):
            c=cells[i]; set_cell_margins(c, 80, 90, 80, 90); c.vertical_alignment=WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT.TOP
            if ridx%2==1: set_cell_shading(c, LIGHT_GRAY)
            p=c.paragraphs[0]; p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(0)
            r=p.add_run(str(val)); r.font.name='Arial'; r.font.size=Pt(font)
    if widths:
        for row in table.rows:
            for i,w in enumerate(widths): row.cells[i].width=Inches(w)
    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(1)
    return table


def add_section_heading(doc, text, level=1):
    p=doc.add_paragraph(text, style=f'Heading {level}')
    keep_with_next(p)
    return p

# ---------------- Redline ----------------
red=Document(); setup(red, 'Seller-Side Markup — Transition Services Agreement', 'TSA Seller-Side Redline')
add_title_block(red, 'SELLER-SIDE REDLINE', 'Trident Manufacturing Group, Inc. draft TSA dated April 28, 2025', 'May 9, 2025')
add_rule(red)
p=red.add_paragraph()
p.add_run('Purpose. ').bold=True
p.add_run('This document presents Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc.\'s proposed seller-side markup of the Trident draft Transition Services Agreement (the “Draft TSA”). It is keyed to the executed APA dated March 14, 2025, including Section 7.12 and Exhibit H, and to Polaris\'s TSA Negotiation Playbook (version 4.2, January 15, 2025).')
p=red.add_paragraph()
p.add_run('Redline convention. ').bold=True
p.add_run('Text shown in red strike-through is proposed for deletion. Text shown in red underline is proposed for addition. The visible comment boxes are the seller-side annotations; each is also anchored as a Word comment to the applicable issue heading. “Firm” identifies a must-change or a Polaris non-negotiable position; “Negotiable” identifies a proposed target with the playbook fallback available.')
add_table(red, ['Priority', 'Meaning', 'Seller-side treatment'], [
    ('CRITICAL', 'APA conflict or board-level exposure', 'Must be corrected before execution; no concession without client escalation.'),
    ('SIGNIFICANT', 'Material playbook deviation or meaningful seller risk', 'Target position shown; fallback identified in comment or memo.'),
    ('MINOR', 'Negotiation preference or cleanup', 'Include in initial markup, but may be traded for value.'),
], widths=[1.1,2.4,3.8])
add_section_heading(red, 'Executive markup summary', 1)
for t in [
    'The Draft TSA contains multiple direct conflicts with APA Section 7.12: the service standard, maximum term/automatic renewal, individual-service termination notice, fee cap/fee mechanics, liability cap, and Mexico cross-border provisions.',
    'The IT fee is 15% rather than the APA-mandated maximum 10%. On the Draft TSA schedule, that overstates the monthly fee by $17,000 and the 18-month aggregate by $306,000.',
    'The Draft TSA gives Trident a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to Polaris\'s enterprise tools, methodologies, software, and know-how. The license must be deleted in full and replaced with an access-only, term-limited provision.',
    'The Draft TSA\'s consequential-damages waiver is unilateral, protecting Trident but not Polaris. The waiver must be mutual and include the APA-aligned third-party indemnity carve-out.',
    'The Draft TSA does not allocate IMMEX certification/reporting responsibility or establish LFPDPPP-compliant data-processing terms for the approximately 300+ Mexican employees at Monterrey.',
]: add_bullet(red, t)
add_section_heading(red, 'Seller-side markup', 1)

# Critical issues
add_issue(red,'C-1','Critical','§3.1 / APA §§7.12(a), (f)','Service standard and lookback',
    'The Draft TSA requires performance “at least equal to or better than” the prior 24-month level and “in all cases” in accordance with industry best practices.',
    'at least equal to or better than the level at which such services were provided to the Business during the twenty-four (24) month period prior to the Closing Date, and in all cases in accordance with industry best practices applicable to each such Service',
    'in a manner and at a level of quality substantially consistent with the manner and level of quality at which such services (or substantially similar services) were provided to or on behalf of the Business during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the Closing Date; provided that Service Provider shall not be required to prioritize the Services over services provided for its own account or retained businesses, or to adopt new methodologies, systems, standards, or best practices not in use for the Business during that period',
    'Firm', 'APA §§7.12(a) and (f) require a 12-month “substantially consistent” benchmark and expressly reject a higher external standard. The playbook rejects “equal to or better than,” 24-month lookbacks, and best-practices overlays.', 'The current text creates a ratcheting service-level floor and potentially requires Polaris to improve or prioritize services for Trident above historical levels, with uncapped dispute and performance risk.')

add_issue(red,'C-2','Critical','§5.2 / APA §7.12(a)','Automatic renewal and maximum term',
    'The Draft TSA automatically renews for up to two additional six-month Renewal Terms unless Polaris sends non-renewal notice 120 days before expiration.',
    'Upon expiration of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive six (6)-month periods ... up to two (2) successive Renewal Terms ... failure by Service Provider to deliver timely notice ... shall result in automatic renewal',
    'This Agreement shall expire at the end of the eighteen (18)-month Initial Term. No automatic renewal or extension shall apply. Any extension of an individual Service must be mutually agreed in a written amendment signed by both Parties, may not exceed six (6) months beyond the Maximum TSA Term for that Service, and shall be priced at cost plus fifteen percent (15%) (subject to the APA); the parties may agree to cost plus ten percent (10%) only as a negotiated fallback.',
    'Firm as to no automatic renewal and written mutual consent; target on extension pricing', 'APA §7.12(a) imposes an 18-month maximum, permits only a mutually signed extension of an individual service for up to six additional months, and expressly prohibits automatic renewal.', 'The Draft TSA can run to 30 months without a bilateral amendment and leaves Polaris locked into below-market pricing while its personnel and systems remain committed to Trident.')

add_issue(red,'C-3','Critical','§5.3 / APA §7.12(c)','Termination notice for individual Services',
    'Either Party must give at least 120 days\' notice to terminate an individual Service.',
    'not less than one hundred twenty (120) days\' prior written notice',
    'not less than ninety (90) days\' prior written notice. The ninety (90)-day period is the minimum and maximum notice period applicable to termination of an individual Service, and shall control over any inconsistent provision of this Agreement.',
    'Firm', 'APA §7.12(c) requires 90 days and states that the period is both a minimum and maximum; the playbook likewise rejects longer notice periods.', 'A 120-day lock-in extends Polaris\'s resource and operational commitment by a third of the APA-approved period and can delay migration or termination when a service is no longer efficient.')

add_issue(red,'C-4','Critical','§6.1, §6.4, Schedule G / APA §7.12(b)','Fee cap, actual-cost adjustment, and fee schedule',
    'The Draft TSA makes Fees the sole fixed compensation for the duration of the Term, prohibits escalation/adjustment, and includes all out-of-pocket costs in the Base Monthly Cost. Schedule B applies a 15% markup to IT.',
    'The Fees represent the sole compensation ... Fees ... are fixed for the duration of the Term ... no additional charges ... IT markup: 15%; Monthly Fee: $391,000',
    'Fees shall be calculated from actual Fully-Loaded Cost plus a uniform markup not exceeding ten percent (10%) for each category. The Fee Schedule is an estimate based on Exhibit H and may be adjusted to reflect actual Fully-Loaded Costs incurred during the Transition Period; no adjustment may exceed the applicable Exhibit H estimate by more than five percent (5%) without Buyer\'s prior written consent. Reasonable direct out-of-pocket costs included in Fully-Loaded Cost shall not be excluded by a “no additional charges” provision. Schedule B: IT markup 10%; Monthly Fee $374,000; Schedule G total monthly fee $1,122,000.',
    'Firm as to the APA 10% ceiling and actual-cost mechanics; negotiable only on administration of estimates', 'APA §7.12(b) caps each category at 10%, requires adjustment for actual Fully-Loaded Cost, permits up to a 5% variance without consent, and defines Fully-Loaded Cost to include reasonable direct out-of-pocket costs. The Draft IT line is over the cap and the fixed-fee language suppresses the APA adjustment mechanism.', 'The 15% IT line creates an immediate $17,000 monthly overcharge and a $306,000 18-month overstatement. Fixed pricing also shifts cost inflation and extraordinary direct costs to Polaris while depriving Polaris of the APA-negotiated adjustment right.')

add_issue(red,'C-5','Critical','§10.1 / APA §7.12(d)','Aggregate liability cap',
    'Polaris\'s aggregate liability is capped at 200% of total Service Charges actually paid under the TSA as of the claim date.',
    'two hundred percent (200%) of the total Service Charges actually paid ... as of the date of the applicable claim',
    'the total TSA Fees actually paid by Service Recipient to Service Provider during the twelve (12)-month period immediately preceding the date on which the applicable claim is first asserted in writing; during the first twelve (12) months, the cap shall equal the TSA Fees actually paid from the Closing Date through the claim date. The cap shall be subject only to the APA §7.12(d) carve-outs, including fraud or willful misconduct, confidentiality breaches, and qualifying third-party indemnification claims.',
    'Firm', 'APA §7.12(d) mandates a rolling trailing-12-month cap and specifies the first-year calculation and carve-outs. The playbook identifies total-fee and multiple-of-total-fee caps as unacceptable.', 'Using the schedules as drafted, Draft fees are $1,139,000/month and an 18-month cap could reach $41,004,000 (200% × $20,502,000). The APA-compliant cap after 12 months is approximately $13,464,000 (12 × $1,122,000), a $27,540,000 reduction. At month 12, the Draft cap is approximately $27,336,000 versus $13,464,000 under the APA, a $13,872,000 delta.')

add_issue(red,'C-6','Critical','§10.2 / APA §7.12(d)','Mutual consequential-damages waiver',
    'Only Service Provider waives consequential, incidental, special, punitive, exemplary, and indirect damages against Service Recipient.',
    'SERVICE PROVIDER HEREBY WAIVES, AND SHALL NOT ASSERT, ANY AND ALL CLAIMS AGAINST SERVICE RECIPIENT ...',
    'NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, INDIRECT, SPECIAL, EXEMPLARY, OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES ... including lost profits, lost revenue, loss of business opportunity, diminution in value, and loss of goodwill; provided that this waiver shall not limit either Party\'s liability for third-party claims for which indemnification is provided under this Agreement, or for fraud, willful misconduct, confidentiality breaches, or IP infringement to the extent applicable.',
    'Firm', 'APA §7.12(d) requires that “either party” be protected. The playbook expressly states that a non-mutual waiver is never acceptable.', 'The unilateral waiver leaves Polaris exposed to Trident\'s consequential-damages theories—business interruption, lost contracts, replacement costs, and supply-chain disruption—while Polaris has already given up its reciprocal claims.')

add_issue(red,'C-7','Critical','§7.1 / Playbook §6.1','Delete perpetual IP license; reserve Polaris IP',
    'The Draft TSA grants Trident a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid-up license, including rights to reproduce, modify, create derivative works, sublicense, and use pre-existing Polaris Materials.',
    'Service Provider hereby grants to Service Recipient a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid-up, non-exclusive license to use, reproduce, modify, adapt, and create derivative works ... including ... sublicense ... and shall survive expiration or termination',
    'All Service Provider Materials remain the sole and exclusive property of Service Provider. No license, sublicense, right, or interest is granted to Service Recipient. During the Term, Service Recipient may access and use Service Provider Materials solely to receive the Services and may not copy, modify, reverse engineer, create derivative works from, or use them outside that purpose. All such access ends immediately upon expiration or termination. Any post-transition license must be separately negotiated for identified materials, restrictions, and compensation.',
    'Firm / non-negotiable', 'The playbook is a firm no-license position because Polaris\'s tools, methodologies, systems, and know-how serve all four divisions. The Draft goes beyond what is needed to receive transitional services.', 'The current language could permanently export enterprise IP, permit sublicensing to Trident successors and assigns, and expose operational know-how used across Polaris\'s retained businesses.')

add_issue(red,'C-8','Critical','§8.4, new §§8.5–8.6 / APA §7.12(g)','Mexico data privacy and IMMEX allocation',
    'Section 8.4 addresses only U.S. data privacy laws. The Draft TSA has no operative allocation of IMMEX certification, reporting, recordkeeping, costs, jeopardy notice, or liability.',
    'Each Party shall comply with all applicable data privacy and data protection laws of the United States ...',

{"command":"python - <<'PY'
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Inches, Pt, RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH, WD_BREAK
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT, WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT
from docx.enum.section import WD_SECTION
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.enum.style import WD_STYLE_TYPE
from docx.enum.text import WD_LINE_SPACING
from docx.enum.section import WD_ORIENT
from docx.enum.table import WD_ROW_HEIGHT_RULE
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime

OUT = Path('output')
OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

NAVY = '17365D'
BLUE = '1F4E79'
RED = 'C00000'
GREEN = '008000'
GRAY = '666666'
LIGHT_BLUE = 'D9EAF7'
LIGHT_GRAY = 'F2F2F2'
LIGHT_YELLOW = 'FFF2CC'
LIGHT_RED = 'FCE4D6'
LIGHT_GREEN = 'E2F0D9'


def set_cell_shading(cell, fill):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = tcPr.find(qn('w:shd'))
    if shd is None:
        shd = OxmlElement('w:shd')
        tcPr.append(shd)
    shd.set(qn('w:fill'), fill)


def set_cell_margins(cell, top=80, start=100, bottom=80, end=100):
    tc = cell._tc
    tcPr = tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    tcMar = tcPr.first_child_found_in('w:tcMar')
    if tcMar is None:
        tcMar = OxmlElement('w:tcMar')
        tcPr.append(tcMar)
    for m, v in [('top', top), ('start', start), ('bottom', bottom), ('end', end)]:
        node = tcMar.find(qn(f'w:{m}'))
        if node is None:
            node = OxmlElement(f'w:{m}')
            tcMar.append(node)
        node.set(qn('w:w'), str(v))
        node.set(qn('w:type'), 'dxa')


def set_cell_border(cell, **kwargs):
    tc = cell._tc
    tcPr = tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    tcBorders = tcPr.first_child_found_in('w:tcBorders')
    if tcBorders is None:
        tcBorders = OxmlElement('w:tcBorders')
        tcPr.append(tcBorders)
    for edge in ('top', 'left', 'bottom', 'right', 'insideH', 'insideV'):
        if edge in kwargs:
            tag = 'w:{}'.format(edge)
            element = tcBorders.find(qn(tag))
            if element is None:
                element = OxmlElement(tag)
                tcBorders.append(element)
            for key in ['val','sz','space','color']:
                if key in kwargs[edge]:
                    element.set(qn('w:{}'.format(key)), str(kwargs[edge][key]))


def set_repeat_table_header(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    tblHeader = OxmlElement('w:tblHeader')
    tblHeader.set(qn('w:val'), 'true')
    trPr.append(tblHeader)


def keep_with_next(p):
    pPr = p._p.get_or_add_pPr()
    k = OxmlElement('w:keepNext')
    pPr.append(k)


def set_keep_together(p):
    pPr = p._p.get_or_add_pPr()
    k = OxmlElement('w:keepLines')
    pPr.append(k)


def add_page_number(paragraph):
    run = paragraph.add_run()
    fldChar1 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); fldChar1.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'begin')
    instrText = OxmlElement('w:instrText'); instrText.set(qn('xml:space'), 'preserve'); instrText.text = 'PAGE'
    fldChar2 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); fldChar2.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'end')
    run._r.append(fldChar1); run._r.append(instrText); run._r.append(fldChar2)


def setup(doc, title, short_title):
    sec = doc.sections[0]

    sec.bottom_margin = Inches(0.7)
    sec.left_margin = Inches(0.8)
    sec.right_margin = Inches(0.8)
    sec.header_distance = Inches(0.3)
    sec.footer_distance = Inches(0.35)
    styles = doc.styles
    styles['Normal'].font.name = 'Arial'; styles['Normal']._element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn('w:eastAsia'), 'Arial'); styles['Normal'].font.size = Pt(9.2)
    styles['Normal'].paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
    styles['Normal'].paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.05
    for sname, size, color in [('Title', 20, NAVY), ('Heading 1', 14, NAVY), ('Heading 2', 11.5, BLUE), ('Heading 3', 10, BLUE)]:
        st = styles[sname]
        st.font.name = 'Arial'; st._element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn('w:eastAsia'), 'Arial'); st.font.size = Pt(size); st.font.bold = True; st.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(color)
        st.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(8); st.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
    for name in ['Redline', 'Callout', 'Small Text', 'Table Text']:
        if name not in styles:
            st = styles.add_style(name, WD_STYLE_TYPE.PARAGRAPH)
        else: st = styles[name]
        st.font.name = 'Arial'; st._element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn('w:eastAsia'), 'Arial')
    styles['Redline'].font.size = Pt(9)
    styles['Redline'].paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
    styles['Callout'].font.size = Pt(8.7)
    styles['Small Text'].font.size = Pt(8)
    styles['Small Text'].font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(GRAY)
    styles['Table Text'].font.size = Pt(8.2)
    # Header/footer
    header = sec.header.paragraphs[0]
    header.text = short_title
    header.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.RIGHT
    for r in header.runs:
        r.font.name = 'Arial'; r.font.size = Pt(8); r.font.italic = True; r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(GRAY)
    footer = sec.footer.paragraphs[0]
    footer.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    r = footer.add_run('PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY-CLIENT WORK PRODUCT   |   ')
    r.font.name = 'Arial'; r.font.size = Pt(8); r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(GRAY)
    r2 = footer.add_run('Page '); r2.font.name='Arial'; r2.font.size=Pt(8); r2.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(GRAY)
    add_page_number(footer)
    # core props
    doc.core_properties.title = title
    doc.core_properties.subject = 'Seller-side review of Trident draft TSA'
    doc.core_properties.author = 'Whitfield & Crane LLP'
    doc.core_properties.comments = 'Prepared for Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc.'


def add_title_block(doc, title, subtitle, date='May 9, 2025'):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    r = p.add_run('PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL\n')
    r.bold=True; r.font.size=Pt(9); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(RED)
    r2 = p.add_run('ATTORNEY-CLIENT WORK PRODUCT')
    r2.bold=True; r2.font.size=Pt(9); r2.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(RED)
    p2 = doc.add_paragraph(style='Title'); p2.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER; p2.add_run(title)
    p3 = doc.add_paragraph(); p3.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    rr=p3.add_run(subtitle); rr.font.size=Pt(10); rr.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(GRAY)
    p4=doc.add_paragraph(); p4.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    rd=p4.add_run(date); rd.font.size=Pt(9); rd.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(GRAY)
    p5=doc.add_paragraph(); p5.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    rr=p5.add_run('Prepared for Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc.'); rr.bold=True; rr.font.size=Pt(9)


def add_rule(doc):
    p=doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(6)
    r=p.add_run('─'*108)
    r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(LIGHT_BLUE); r.font.size=Pt(5)


def add_bullet(doc, text, level=0, bold_prefix=None):
    p=doc.add_paragraph(style='Normal')
    p.paragraph_format.left_indent=Inches(0.22+0.18*level)
    p.paragraph_format.first_line_indent=Inches(-0.15)
    p.add_run('• ').bold=True
    if bold_prefix and text.startswith(bold_prefix):
        p.add_run(bold_prefix).bold=True; p.add_run(text[len(bold_prefix):])
    else: p.add_run(text)
    return p


def add_redline_para(doc, label, deleted=None, added=None, note=None):
    p=doc.add_paragraph(style='Redline')
    p.paragraph_format.left_indent=Inches(0.15)
    rr=p.add_run(label + ' '); rr.bold=True; rr.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(BLUE)
    if deleted:
        d=p.add_run(deleted); d.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(RED); d.font.strike=True
    if deleted and added:
        sep=p.add_run('  →  '); sep.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(GRAY)
    if added:
        a=p.add_run(added); a.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(RED); a.font.underline=True
    if note:
        n=p.add_run('  ' + note); n.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(GRAY); n.font.italic=True
    return p


def add_current(doc, text):
    p=doc.add_paragraph(style='Small Text')
    p.paragraph_format.left_indent=Inches(0.15)
    r=p.add_run('Draft: '); r.bold=True; r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(GRAY)
    p.add_run(text)
    return p


def add_comment_callout(doc, code, priority, position, basis, risk, comment_id=None, anchor=None):
    table=doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=1)
    table.alignment=WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    cell=table.cell(0,0); cell.vertical_alignment=WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    fill = LIGHT_RED if priority=='Critical' else LIGHT_YELLOW if priority=='Significant' else LIGHT_BLUE
    set_cell_shading(cell, fill); set_cell_margins(cell, 100, 130, 100, 130)
    set_cell_border(cell, top={'val':'single','sz':'6','color':'A6A6A6'}, bottom={'val':'single','sz':'6','color':'A6A6A6'}, left={'val':'single','sz':'12','color':RED if priority=='Critical' else BLUE}, right={'val':'single','sz':'6','color':'A6A6A6'})
    p=cell.paragraphs[0]; p.style='Callout'; p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(2)
    r=p.add_run(f'Comment {code} — {priority} — {position}'); r.bold=True; r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(RED if priority=='Critical' else BLUE)
    for label, val in [('Basis', basis), ('Risk', risk)]:
        pp=cell.add_paragraph(style='Callout'); pp.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(1)
        rr=pp.add_run(label + ': '); rr.bold=True
        pp.add_run(val)
    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(1)
    return table


def add_issue(doc, code, priority, section, title, current, deleted, added, position, basis, risk, extra=None):
    p=doc.add_paragraph(style='Heading 2')
    r=p.add_run(f'{code}  |  {priority.upper()}  |  {section} — {title}')
    keep_with_next(p)
    comment_text=f'{priority} / {position}. Basis: {basis} Risk: {risk}'
    c=doc.comments.add_comment(comment_text, author='Polaris Seller\'s Counsel', initials='PSC')
    r.mark_comment_range(r, c.comment_id)
    add_current(doc, current)
    add_redline_para(doc, 'DELETE', deleted=deleted)
    add_redline_para(doc, 'ADD', added=added)
    add_comment_callout(doc, code, priority, position, basis, risk)
    if extra:
        p=doc.add_paragraph(style='Small Text'); p.add_run(extra)
    return p


def add_table(doc, headers, rows, widths=None, font=8.2):

    for i,h in enumerate(headers):
        c=hdr.cells[i]; set_cell_shading(c, NAVY); set_cell_margins(c, 90, 90, 90, 90); c.vertical_alignment=WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
        p=c.paragraphs[0]; p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(0); p.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
        r=p.add_run(h); r.bold=True; r.font.name='Arial'; r.font.size=Pt(font); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(255,255,255)
    for ridx,row in enumerate(rows):
        cells=table.add_row().cells
        for i,val in enumerate(row):
            c=cells[i]; set_cell_margins(c, 80, 90, 80, 90); c.vertical_alignment=WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT.TOP

            r=p.add_run(str(val)); r.font.name='Arial'; r.font.size=Pt(font)
    if widths:
        for row in table.rows:
            for i,w in enumerate(widths): row.cells[i].width=Inches(w)

    return table


def add_section_heading(doc, text, level=1):

It is keyed to the executed APA dated March 14, 2025, including Section 7.12 and Exhibit H, and to Polaris\'s TSA Negotiation Playbook (version 4.2, January 15, 2025).')
p=red.add_paragraph()
p.add_run('Redline convention. ').bold=True

The visible comment boxes are the seller-side annotations; each is also anchored as a Word comment to the applicable issue heading. “Firm” identifies a must-change or a Polaris non-negotiable position; “Negotiable” identifies a proposed target with the playbook fallback available.')
add_table(red, ['Priority', 'Meaning', 'Seller-side treatment'], [
    ('CRITICAL', 'APA conflict or board-level exposure', 'Must be corrected before execution; no concession without client escalation.'),

for t in [

    'The Draft TSA gives Trident a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to Polaris\'s enterprise tools, methodologies, software, and know-how. The license must be deleted in full and replaced with an access-only, term-limited provision.',
    'The Draft TSA\'s consequential-damages waiver is unilateral, protecting Trident but not Polaris. The waiver must be mutual and include the APA-aligned third-party indemnity carve-out.',
    'The Draft TSA does not allocate IMMEX certification/reporting responsibility or establish LFPDPPP-compliant data-processing terms for the approximately 300+ Mexican employees at Monterrey.',

add_section_heading(red, 'Seller-side markup', 1)

# Critical issues
add_issue(red,'C-1','Critical','§3.1 / APA §§7.12(a), (f)','Service standard and lookback',
    'The Draft TSA requires performance “at least equal to or better than” the prior 24-month level and “in all cases” in accordance with industry best practices.',
    'at least equal to or better than the level at which such services were provided to the Business during the twenty-four (24) month period prior to the Closing Date, and in all cases in accordance with industry best practices applicable to each such Service',
    'in a manner and at a level of quality substantially consistent with the manner and level of quality at which such services (or substantially similar services) were provided to or on behalf of the Business during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the Closing Date; provided that Service Provider shall not be required to prioritize the Services over services provided for its own account or retained businesses, or to adopt new methodologies, systems, standards, or best practices not in use for the Business during that period',
    'Firm', 'APA §§7.12(a) and (f) require a 12-month “substantially consistent” benchmark and expressly reject a higher external standard. The playbook rejects “equal to or better than,” 24-month lookbacks, and best-practices overlays.', 'The current text creates a ratcheting service-level floor and potentially requires Polaris to improve or prioritize services for Trident above historical levels, with uncapped dispute and performance risk.')

add_issue(red,'C-2','Critical','§5.2 / APA §7.12(a)','Automatic renewal and maximum term',
    'The Draft TSA automatically renews for up to two additional six-month Renewal Terms unless Polaris sends non-renewal notice 120 days before expiration.',
    'Upon expiration of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive six (6)-month periods ... up to two (2) successive Renewal Terms ... failure by Service Provider to deliver timely notice ... shall result in automatic renewal',
    'This Agreement shall expire at the end of the eighteen (18)-month Initial Term. No automatic renewal or extension shall apply. Any extension of an individual Service must be mutually agreed in a written amendment signed by both Parties, may not exceed six (6) months beyond the Maximum TSA Term for that Service, and shall be priced at cost plus fifteen percent (15%) (subject to the APA); the parties may agree to cost plus ten percent (10%) only as a negotiated fallback.',
    'Firm as to no automatic renewal and written mutual consent; target on extension pricing', 'APA §7.12(a) imposes an 18-month maximum, permits only a mutually signed extension of an individual service for up to six additional months, and expressly prohibits automatic renewal.', 'The Draft TSA can run to 30 months without a bilateral amendment and leaves Polaris locked into below-market pricing while its personnel and systems remain committed to Trident.')

add_issue(red,'C-3','Critical','§5.3 / APA §7.12(c)','Termination notice for individual Services',
    'Either Party must give at least 120 days\' notice to terminate an individual Service.',
    'not less than one hundred twenty (120) days\' prior written notice',
    'not less than ninety (90) days\' prior written notice. The ninety (90)-day period is the minimum and maximum notice period applicable to termination of an individual Service, and shall control over any inconsistent provision of this Agreement.',
    'Firm', 'APA §7.12(c) requires 90 days and states that the period is both a minimum and maximum; the playbook likewise rejects longer notice periods.', 'A 120-day lock-in extends Polaris\'s resource and operational commitment by a third of the APA-approved period and can delay migration or termination when a service is no longer efficient.')

add_issue(red,'C-4','Critical','§6.1, §6.4, Schedule G / APA §7.12(b)','Fee cap, actual-cost adjustment, and fee schedule',
    'The Draft TSA makes Fees the sole fixed compensation for the duration of the Term, prohibits escalation/adjustment, and includes all out-of-pocket costs in the Base Monthly Cost. Schedule B applies a 15% markup to IT.',
    'The Fees represent the sole compensation ... Fees ... are fixed for the duration of the Term ... no additional charges ... IT markup: 15%; Monthly Fee: $391,000',
    'Fees shall be calculated from actual Fully-Loaded Cost plus a uniform markup not exceeding ten percent (10%) for each category. The Fee Schedule is an estimate based on Exhibit H and may be adjusted to reflect actual Fully-Loaded Costs incurred during the Transition Period; no adjustment may exceed the applicable Exhibit H estimate by more than five percent (5%) without Buyer\'s prior written consent. Reasonable direct out-of-pocket costs included in Fully-Loaded Cost shall not be excluded by a “no additional charges” provision. Schedule B: IT markup 10%; Monthly Fee $374,000; Schedule G total monthly fee $1,122,000.',
    'Firm as to the APA 10% ceiling and actual-cost mechanics; negotiable only on administration of estimates', 'APA §7.12(b) caps each category at 10%, requires adjustment for actual Fully-Loaded Cost, permits up to a 5% variance without consent, and defines Fully-Loaded Cost to include reasonable direct out-of-pocket costs. The Draft IT line is over the cap and the fixed-fee language suppresses the APA adjustment mechanism.', 'The 15% IT line creates an immediate $17,000 monthly overcharge and a $306,000 18-month overstatement. Fixed pricing also shifts cost inflation and extraordinary direct costs to Polaris while depriving Polaris of the APA-negotiated adjustment right.')

add_issue(red,'C-5','Critical','§10.1 / APA §7.12(d)','Aggregate liability cap',
    'Polaris\'s aggregate liability is capped at 200% of total Service Charges actually paid under the TSA as of the claim date.',
    'two hundred percent (200%) of the total Service Charges actually paid ... as of the date of the applicable claim',
    'the total TSA Fees actually paid by Service Recipient to Service Provider during the twelve (12)-month period immediately preceding the date on which the applicable claim is first asserted in writing; during the first twelve (12) months, the cap shall equal the TSA Fees actually paid from the Closing Date through the claim date. The cap shall be subject only to the APA §7.12(d) carve-outs, including fraud or willful misconduct, confidentiality breaches, and qualifying third-party indemnification claims.',
    'Firm', 'APA §7.12(d) mandates a rolling trailing-12-month cap and specifies the first-year calculation and carve-outs. The playbook identifies total-fee and multiple-of-total-fee caps as unacceptable.', 'Using the schedules as drafted, Draft fees are $1,139,000/month and an 18-month cap could reach $41,004,000 (200% × $20,502,000). The APA-compliant cap after 12 months is approximately $13,464,000 (12 × $1,122,000), a $27,540,000 reduction. At month 12, the Draft cap is approximately $27,336,000 versus $13,464,000 under the APA, a $13,872,000 delta.')

add_issue(red,'C-6','Critical','§10.2 / APA §7.12(d)','Mutual consequential-damages waiver',
    'Only Service Provider waives consequential, incidental, special, punitive, exemplary, and indirect damages against Service Recipient.',
    'SERVICE PROVIDER HEREBY WAIVES, AND SHALL NOT ASSERT, ANY AND ALL CLAIMS AGAINST SERVICE RECIPIENT ...',
    'NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, INDIRECT, SPECIAL, EXEMPLARY, OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES ... including lost profits, lost revenue, loss of business opportunity, diminution in value, and loss of goodwill; provided that this waiver shall not limit either Party\'s liability for third-party claims for which indemnification is provided under this Agreement, or for fraud, willful misconduct, confidentiality breaches, or IP infringement to the extent applicable.',
    'Firm', 'APA §7.12(d) requires that “either party” be protected. The playbook expressly states that a non-mutual waiver is never acceptable.', 'The unilateral waiver leaves Polaris exposed to Trident\'s consequential-damages theories—business interruption, lost contracts, replacement costs, and supply-chain disruption—while Polaris has already given up its reciprocal claims.')

add_issue(red,'C-7','Critical','§7.1 / Playbook §6.1','Delete perpetual IP license; reserve Polaris IP',
    'The Draft TSA grants Trident a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid-up license, including rights to reproduce, modify, create derivative works, sublicense, and use pre-existing Polaris Materials.',
    'Service Provider hereby grants to Service Recipient a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid-up, non-exclusive license to use, reproduce, modify, adapt, and create derivative works ... including ... sublicense ... and shall survive expiration or termination',
    'All Service Provider Materials remain the sole and exclusive property of Service Provider. No license, sublicense, right, or interest is granted to Service Recipient. During the Term, Service Recipient may access and use Service Provider Materials solely to receive the Services and may not copy, modify, reverse engineer, create derivative works from, or use them outside that purpose. All such access ends immediately upon expiration or termination. Any post-transition license must be separately negotiated for identified materials, restrictions, and compensation.',
    'Firm / non-negotiable', 'The playbook is a firm no-license position because Polaris\'s tools, methodologies, systems, and know-how serve all four divisions. The Draft goes beyond what is needed to receive transitional services.', 'The current language could permanently export enterprise IP, permit sublicensing to Trident successors and assigns, and expose operational know-how used across Polaris\'s retained businesses.')

add_issue(red,'C-8','Critical','§8.4, new §§8.5–8.6 / APA §7.12(g)','Mexico data privacy and IMMEX allocation',
    'Section 8.4 addresses only U.S. data privacy laws. The Draft TSA has no operative allocation of IMMEX certification, reporting, recordkeeping, costs, jeopardy notice, or liability.',
    'Each Party shall comply with all applicable data privacy and data protection laws of the United States ...',
    'Each Party shall comply with all applicable data privacy and data protection laws, expressly including Mexico\'s LFPDPPP and its Regulations. For Mexico employee data, Trident is the controller and Polaris is the processor/service provider acting only on Trident\'s documented instructions. Trident shall provide and maintain legally sufficient avisos de privacidad, notices, consents, and cross-border transfer mechanisms before data is transferred to or processed by Polaris. Polaris shall maintain appropriate safeguards, limit processing to the Services, notify Trident without undue delay and, where practicable, within twenty-four (24) hours after becoming aware of a security incident, assist with required response, use equivalent protections for subprocessors, and return or delete data at termination subject to law. Trident, as post-Closing operator, has primary responsibility for obtaining and maintaining IMMEX certification, required reports, temporary-import records, customs/trade compliance, and associated costs. Polaris shall provide only the transition assistance expressly described in Schedule E and shall not be responsible for Trident\'s failure to obtain or maintain certification. Each Party shall notify the other promptly if it learns that IMMEX status is or may be jeopardized and shall cooperate to avoid a lapse.',
    'Firm as to inclusion and allocation; technical implementation negotiable with local counsel', 'APA §7.12(g) expressly requires Mexican-law provisions addressing IMMEX certification/reporting and LFPDPPP lawful basis, privacy notices, and safeguards. The client instructions identify the 300+ Monterrey employees and IMMEX exposure as a priority.', 'Without allocation, Polaris may be treated as responsible for Trident\'s post-Closing certification, customs, or privacy failures, with duty/tax, enforcement, payroll, and operational disruption risk. The added terms give Trident primary control and responsibility while preserving defined, compensated transition assistance.')

add_issue(red,'C-9','Critical','§9.1–§9.2 / APA §7.12(d)','Narrow indemnities and align with cap',
    'The Draft provides broad indemnification for all Losses, including direct claims for breach and any violation of Applicable Law by Polaris, but does not state that indemnities are limited to third-party claims or align them to the APA cap/carve-outs.',
    'Service Provider shall indemnify ... from and against any and all Losses ... any breach ... or any violation of Applicable Law ...',
    'Service Recipient shall indemnify Service Provider Indemnitees against third-party claims arising from Service Recipient\'s use of or reliance on the Services, except to the extent caused by Service Provider\'s gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct. Service Provider\'s indemnity shall be limited to third-party claims arising from Service Provider\'s gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct in performing the Services. The indemnities shall be subject to the APA §7.12(d) liability structure, including the applicable third-party-claim carve-out, and shall not create a separate uncapped direct-loss remedy.',
    'Firm on scope and third-party limitation; APA carve-out controls', 'The playbook limits indemnity to third-party claims and uses a gross-negligence/willful-misconduct threshold. APA §7.12(d) supplies the exclusive TSA cap and specific third-party indemnity treatment.', 'As written, Trident could recast ordinary service disputes, contractual breaches, or regulatory issues as uncapped indemnity claims, bypassing the negotiated liability allocation.')

add_issue(red,'C-10','Critical','§2.1, §4.3, Schedule H / Exhibit H General Notes','Staffing estimates; no buyer consent over Polaris personnel',
    'The Draft allocates approximately 100 FTEs by category and requires Schedule H Key Personnel to remain at minimum FTE allocations. Reassignment, transfer, termination, replacement, or reductions require Trident\'s prior written consent.',
    'Service Provider shall ensure ... Key Personnel ... at the FTE allocation levels ... shall not reassign ... without the prior written consent of Service Recipient ... minimum commitment',
    'FTE counts and personnel assignments are estimates only and may be adjusted by Service Provider in its reasonable discretion, provided that Service Provider allocates sufficient reasonably qualified resources to meet the Service Standard. Service Provider retains sole discretion over staffing, assignment, reassignment, promotion, transfer, replacement, and termination. Service Provider shall provide fifteen (15) Business Days\' advance notice before reassigning or replacing personnel on a mutually agreed notice list and shall assign a reasonably qualified replacement; no Service Recipient consent is required.',
    'Firm on sole discretion; 15-business-day notice is negotiable', 'Exhibit H says FTE counts are estimates adjustable by Seller in its reasonable discretion. The playbook rejects buyer consent over Key Personnel and protects operational flexibility.', 'The Draft gives Trident veto power over Polaris employment decisions and converts estimates into hard staffing commitments, impairing Polaris\'s ability to serve its retained divisions and creating employment-law and continuity risk.')

add_section_heading(red, 'Significant playbook deviations and seller protections', 1)
add_issue(red,'S-1','Significant','§5.5–§5.6 / Playbook §3.4','Termination assistance / wind-down',
    'The Draft TSA ends the Service Provider obligation at termination and contains no defined, compensated termination-assistance period.',
    'Service Provider\'s obligation to provide the terminated or expired Services shall immediately cease ... all rights and obligations ... shall cease',
    'Upon expiration or termination of a Service, Service Provider shall provide reasonable termination assistance for no more than sixty (60) days, limited to knowledge transfer, data migration support, cooperation with a replacement provider, and transition documentation, at cost plus fifteen percent (15%) (cost plus ten percent (10%) is the maximum fallback). No assistance is required while Service Recipient has unpaid undisputed invoices or if the requested assistance would violate law, a third-party agreement, or Polaris\'s confidentiality obligations.',
    'Negotiable; 60 days / 15% target, 90 days / 10% fallback', 'The playbook requires a defined wind-down to avoid implied indefinite cooperation and to compensate Polaris for post-termination burden.', 'Silence invites disputes over implied duties and could require Polaris to support Trident indefinitely without payment or resource limits.')

add_issue(red,'S-2','Significant','New §6.7; §2.2 / Playbook §4.4','Formal change-order procedure',
    'Section 2.2 says scope changes must be mutually agreed in writing but does not require a signed change order, price out-of-scope work, or preserve Polaris\'s discretion to decline.',
    'no expansion, modification, or enhancement ... except as may be mutually agreed in writing',
    'Any out-of-scope service, material volume increase, or material scope change requires a written change order signed by authorized representatives of both Parties. Change-order pricing shall be cost plus fifteen percent (15%) (cost plus ten percent (10%) fallback). Acceptance is in Service Provider\'s sole discretion; Service Provider has no obligation to perform until the change order is executed and any required advance payment is received. Additional Services may be priced above 10% only as permitted by APA §7.12(b).',
    'Negotiable on price; firm on written dual signature and no obligation before execution', 'The playbook requires a formal change-order process to prevent scope creep; APA §7.12(b) permits mutually agreed Additional Services pricing.', 'Informal requests could expand service scope without compensation or create an argument that expanded work is included in fixed Fees.')

add_issue(red,'S-3','Significant','§6.3 / Playbook §4.3','Payment terms and late interest',
    'Undisputed invoices are payable within a “commercially reasonable time,” with no late-interest remedy.',
    'within a commercially reasonable time following receipt thereof',
    'within thirty (30) days after the date of invoice (Net 30). Overdue amounts shall accrue interest at the lesser of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month or the maximum rate permitted by law. Service Recipient shall pay all undisputed portions when due notwithstanding a dispute over another portion.',
    'Negotiable to Net 45; late-interest floor 1.0%/month', 'The playbook rejects vague payment timing and requires specific Net 30 terms and interest.', 'Ambiguity delays cash collection and weakens enforcement; Trident could withhold undisputed amounts while escalating a narrow invoice dispute.')

add_issue(red,'S-4','Significant','§6.4 / Schedule G / Playbook §4.2','Fee escalation and cost events',
    'Fees are fixed for the entire Term and any Renewal Terms, with no annual escalation or escalation-event mechanism.',
    'Fees ... are fixed for the duration of the Term and shall not be subject to escalation or adjustment',
    'On each anniversary of the Closing Date, Fees shall increase by the greater of three percent (3%) or the trailing twelve-month CPI-U increase, in each case subject to the APA fee cap. Fees may also be adjusted through a written change order or escalation event for material cost increases caused by a change in law, regulation, vendor pricing, or a material volume/scope increase requested by Service Recipient.',
    'Negotiable; CPI-U only is fallback, but retain escalation-event protection', 'The playbook targets a 3% floor/CPI-U escalation and an escalation-event mechanism because Polaris is providing an accommodation, not a long-term below-market service business. APA actual-cost and 10% markup limits remain controlling.', 'Fixed pricing creates a negative migration incentive and leaves Polaris bearing inflation, vendor, legal, and volume-driven costs during the transition.')

add_issue(red,'S-5','Significant','§14.1–§14.2 / Playbook §9','Audit scope, frequency, notice, and cost',
    'Trident may audit twice per calendar year at Polaris\'s expense, on 10 business days\' notice, with access to systems and supporting documentation. Any overcharge must be repaid with interest.',
    'at Service Provider\'s expense ... up to two (2) times per calendar year ... ten (10) Business Days ... books, records, systems ... Service Provider\'s expense',
    'Service Recipient may audit fee-related books and records once in any twelve (12)-month period, at its sole expense, on thirty (30) Business Days\' prior written notice, during normal business hours. Audits exclude proprietary systems, internal cost methodologies, unrelated personnel records, and data of other Polaris businesses. If an audit shows an overcharge exceeding five percent (5%) for the audited period, Polaris shall reimburse the overcharge and reasonable audit costs; otherwise each Party bears its own costs.',
    'Negotiable to twice during the TSA term, 20 business days\' notice; firm on scope and seller not default payer', 'The playbook limits frequency, requires 30-business-day notice, places audit cost on Trident, and uses a 5% threshold.', 'The Draft invites disruptive and potentially frivolous audits, exposes Polaris systems and other divisions, and automatically shifts audit expense to Polaris.')

add_issue(red,'S-6','Significant','§13.1 / Playbook §8','Buyer insurance and additional insured protection',
    'Trident must maintain only $2 million CGL coverage, with no umbrella, additional-insured endorsement, waiver of subrogation, or certificate delivery deadline.',
    'commercial general liability insurance ... $2,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 annual aggregate',
    'CGL of $5,000,000 per occurrence and aggregate; umbrella/excess of $5,000,000; workers\' compensation at statutory limits; Polaris named as additional insured under CGL and umbrella; waiver of subrogation in favor of Polaris; certificates delivered within ten (10) Business Days after Closing and annually thereafter. Coverage continues through the Term and for twelve (12) months after termination.',
    'Negotiable to $3M CGL/$3M umbrella as absolute minimum; never omit additional insured', 'The playbook calls for $5M CGL, $5M umbrella, statutory workers\' compensation, additional-insured status, waiver of subrogation, and certificate delivery.', 'The $2M-only requirement is inadequate for industrial coatings/manufacturing risks and gives Polaris no direct policy protection or evidence of coverage.')

add_issue(red,'S-7','Significant','§12.1–§12.2 / Playbook §10','Force majeure termination trigger',
    'The Draft excuses delay, requires notice/mitigation, and permits fee adjustment, but has no exit right after a prolonged force majeure event and does not expressly include cyberattacks.',
    'Neither Party shall be liable ... [no termination trigger]',
    'If a Force Majeure Event continues for ninety (90) consecutive days and materially prevents performance of an affected Service, either Party may terminate that affected Service on written notice without penalty. Fees remain payable for Services actually delivered through termination. “Force Majeure Event” expressly includes cyberattacks and material internet/telecommunications outages.',
    'Negotiable to a 120-day trigger; never omit the trigger', 'The playbook requires a 90-day termination trigger and includes cyberattacks among covered events.', 'Polaris could remain obligated to resume a service indefinitely after a prolonged disruption, even where systems, vendors, or resource allocation have materially changed.')

add_issue(red,'S-8','Significant','§15.1–§15.2 / Playbook §11','Pennsylvania law and AAA arbitration in Pittsburgh',
    'The Draft selects Ohio law and exclusive litigation in Cuyahoga County, Ohio, with a jury waiver.',
    'laws of the State of Ohio ... exclusively in the state or federal courts located in Cuyahoga County, Ohio',
    'This Agreement shall be governed by Pennsylvania law, without regard to conflicts principles. Disputes shall first be escalated to designated CFO/General Counsel-level executives for fifteen (15) Business Days, then may proceed to non-binding mediation, and finally shall be resolved by confidential binding arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association under its Commercial Arbitration Rules in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania before one arbitrator with relevant industry experience. No litigation mechanism shall apply except to enforce an award or obtain provisional relief.',
    'Firm target; Delaware law / Philadelphia or New York arbitration are playbook fallbacks', 'The playbook targets Pennsylvania law and AAA arbitration in Pittsburgh; the Draft gives Trident a home-state forum and public litigation.', 'Ohio litigation creates home-court, public-docket, discovery, and procedural exposure for a Pittsburgh-based service provider.')

add_issue(red,'S-9','Significant','New §15.12 / Playbook §7.2','Non-solicitation of Polaris personnel',
    'The Draft contains no non-solicitation covenant.',
    'No corresponding provision',
    'During the Term and for twelve (12) months after expiration or termination, Service Recipient shall not, without Polaris\'s prior written consent, solicit, recruit, hire, or engage any Polaris employee who provided Services. Exceptions apply to general solicitations not targeted at Polaris personnel and individuals terminated by Polaris without cause. Six months is the absolute minimum fallback.',
    'Negotiable on post-term duration; firm on a term restriction', 'The playbook requires coverage for all service-providing employees, not only Key Personnel, to prevent buyer cherry-picking and depletion of Polaris\'s shared-services workforce.', 'Trident will gain detailed knowledge of Polaris\'s most effective shared-services personnel and could hire them, impairing Polaris\'s ability to support its remaining divisions and the TSA itself.')

add_issue(red,'S-10','Significant','§5.4 / Playbook §3.3','Termination for cause, insolvency, and non-payment',
    'The Draft has a 30-day cure period that can extend to 90 days and lacks immediate Polaris termination rights for insolvency, prolonged non-payment, or material legal/regulatory/reputational risk.',
    'no cure period shall extend beyond ninety (90) days',
    'Either Party may terminate for material breach uncured within thirty (30) days (forty-five (45) days is the maximum fallback). Polaris may terminate immediately upon Trident insolvency or bankruptcy, failure to pay undisputed amounts more than sixty (60) days past due, or conduct creating material legal, regulatory, or reputational risk to Polaris.',
    'Negotiable on cure period; firm on insolvency and non-payment rights', 'The playbook calls for a 30-day cure period (45-day fallback) and immediate provider termination rights for insolvency and non-payment.', 'A 90-day cure tail can force Polaris to continue service while unpaid or while Trident conduct exposes Polaris to legal or reputational harm.')

add_issue(red,'S-11','Significant','Schedules A–F / Exhibit H','Limit schedule scope to Exhibit H; remove embedded scope creep',
    'Several schedules expand or harden the service obligation beyond Exhibit H or introduce open-ended tasks: Tier 3 SAP support and industry-standard cybersecurity language; new-hire onboarding; tax provision/transfer-pricing work; continuing warehouse allocation; and broad “other reports” and filing obligations.',
    'Tier 2 and Tier 3 SAP application support ... industry-standard practices ... New Hire Onboarding Support ... Tax Provision Support ... Transfer Pricing Documentation Support ... existing allocation ... shall continue',
    'Each Schedule is limited to the applicable service category and description in Exhibit H and the historical service level. Any service not expressly described in Exhibit H, including Tier 3/custom development, new-hire onboarding, tax provision or transfer-pricing studies, expanded filing obligations, or continuing warehouse commitments, is an Additional Service requiring a signed change order and separate pricing. No warehouse sharing or access obligation continues unless a separate written arrangement is executed.',
    'Firm on no unpriced scope expansion; specific scope trades are negotiable through change order', 'APA §7.12 and Exhibit H define the contemplated services, and the playbook rejects scope creep without a written change order.', 'Open-ended schedule language could require Polaris to provide new professional services, custom IT work, or facility commitments without the staffing, third-party consents, or compensation contemplated by the APA.')

add_section_heading(red, 'Minor / cleanup positions', 1)
add_issue(red,'M-1','Minor','§7.2–§7.3 / Playbook §6.2','Data ownership and transition return',
    'Section 7.2 addresses only Trident-provided materials and requires destruction at termination; it does not reserve Polaris system-level/pre-Closing data or state that Trident owns post-Closing Buyer Data subject to migration.',

add_issue(red,'M-2','Minor','§1.1, §5.2, §5.6 / Conforming changes','Delete Renewal Term and conform survival/definitions',
    'The Draft defines Renewal Term and Term as Initial Term plus Renewal Terms and makes the renewal concept operative in Schedule G.',
    '“Renewal Term” ... each successive six (6)-month period ... “Term” means the Initial Term plus any Renewal Terms',
    'Delete “Renewal Term.” “Term” means the Initial Term, together with any individual-service extension documented under §5.1 and APA §7.12(a). Update all references to “Renewal Term” and fixed fees during Renewal Terms to conform to the no-automatic-renewal structure.',

add_issue(red,'M-3','Minor','§2.2, §3.3, Schedule assumptions / Playbook §§2.2, 4.4','Operational exclusions and dependencies',
    'The Draft has helpful scope limitations and cooperation language but omits express exclusions for legal/tax/strategic advice, third-party contract breaches, and changes made to Polaris-wide systems, and does not clearly tie volume changes to change-order pricing.',

    'Negotiable wording; risk allocation is important', 'These are standard playbook exclusions and track APA §7.12(e)(i)–(iv).', 'The current drafting may turn reasonable operational changes or third-party licensing constraints into service breaches.')

add_issue(red,'M-4','Minor','§14.2 / Playbook §9','Audit adjustment mechanics',
    'The Draft requires repayment of any overcharge with interest but does not provide a reciprocal payment for undercharges or a 5% threshold.',
    'If an audit ... reveals that Service Provider has overcharged ... credit the amount ... together with interest',
    'If an audit identifies an overcharge exceeding five percent (5%) for the audited period, Polaris shall credit the overcharge and reasonable audit costs. If an audit identifies an undercharge, Trident shall pay the undercharge within thirty (30) days. No interest applies unless the audited party fails to pay a determined amount when due.',
