**PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL\
ATTORNEY-CLIENT WORK PRODUCT**

SELLER-SIDE REDLINE

Trident Manufacturing Group, Inc. draft TSA dated April 28, 2025

May 9, 2025

**Prepared for Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc.**

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

**Purpose.** This document presents Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc.\'s proposed seller-side markup of the Trident draft Transition Services Agreement (the "Draft TSA"). It is keyed to the executed APA dated March 14, 2025, including Section 7.12 and Exhibit H, and to Polaris\'s TSA Negotiation Playbook (version 4.2, January 15, 2025).

**Redline convention.** Text shown in red strike-through is proposed for deletion. Text shown in red underline is proposed for addition. The visible comment boxes are the seller-side annotations; each is also anchored as a Word comment to the applicable issue heading. "Firm" identifies a must-change or a Polaris non-negotiable position; "Negotiable" identifies a proposed target with the playbook fallback available.

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
       **Priority**       **Meaning**                                             **Seller-side treatment**
  ----------------------- ------------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
         CRITICAL         APA conflict or board-level exposure                    Must be corrected before execution; no concession without client escalation.

        SIGNIFICANT       Material playbook deviation or meaningful seller risk   Target position shown; fallback identified in comment or memo.

           MINOR          Negotiation preference or cleanup                       Include in initial markup, but may be traded for value.
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Executive markup summary

> **•** The Draft TSA contains multiple direct conflicts with APA Section 7.12: the service standard, maximum term/automatic renewal, individual-service termination notice, fee cap/fee mechanics, liability cap, and Mexico cross-border provisions.
>
> **•** The IT fee is 15% rather than the APA-mandated maximum 10%. On the Draft TSA schedule, that overstates the monthly fee by \$17,000 and the 18-month aggregate by \$306,000.
>
> **•** The Draft TSA gives Trident a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to Polaris\'s enterprise tools, methodologies, software, and know-how. The license must be deleted in full and replaced with an access-only, term-limited provision.
>
> **•** The Draft TSA\'s consequential-damages waiver is unilateral, protecting Trident but not Polaris. The waiver must be mutual and include the APA-aligned third-party indemnity carve-out.
>
> **•** The Draft TSA does not allocate IMMEX certification/reporting responsibility or establish LFPDPPP-compliant data-processing terms for the approximately 300+ Mexican employees at Monterrey.

# Seller-side markup

## C-1 \| CRITICAL \| §3.1 / APA §§7.12(a), (f) --- Service standard and lookback

> **Draft:** The Draft TSA requires performance "at least equal to or better than" the prior 24-month level and "in all cases" in accordance with industry best practices.
>
> **DELETE** ~~at least equal to or better than the level at which such services were provided to the Business during the twenty-four (24) month period prior to the Closing Date, and in all cases in accordance with industry best practices applicable to each such Service~~
>
> **ADD** [in a manner and at a level of quality substantially consistent with the manner and level of quality at which such services (or substantially similar services) were provided to or on behalf of the Business during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the Closing Date; provided that Service Provider shall not be required to prioritize the Services over services provided for its own account or retained businesses, or to adopt new methodologies, systems, standards, or best practices not in use for the Business during that period]{.underline}

+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **Comment C-1 --- Critical --- Firm**                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **Basis:** APA §§7.12(a) and (f) require a 12-month "substantially consistent" benchmark and expressly reject a higher external standard. The playbook rejects "equal to or better than," 24-month lookbacks, and best-practices overlays. |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **Risk:** The current text creates a ratcheting service-level floor and potentially requires Polaris to improve or prioritize services for Trident above historical levels, with uncapped dispute and performance risk.                    |
+============================================================================================================================================================================================================================================+

## C-2 \| CRITICAL \| §5.2 / APA §7.12(a) --- Automatic renewal and maximum term

> **Draft:** The Draft TSA automatically renews for up to two additional six-month Renewal Terms unless Polaris sends non-renewal notice 120 days before expiration.
>

**PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL\
ATTORNEY-CLIENT WORK PRODUCT**

COVER MEMORANDUM

Seller-side review of Trident draft Transition Services Agreement

May 9, 2025

**Prepared for Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc.**

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                **To**                **Victoria S. Andersen, Partner**
  ----------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                 From                 Nathan J. Reeves, Whitfield & Crane LLP

                  Re                  Polaris / Trident --- Specialty Coatings Divestiture --- Draft TSA review

          Documents reviewed          Trident Draft TSA (Apr. 28, 2025); APA (Mar. 14, 2025) §§7.12, 12.3, 12.5 and Exhibit H excerpts; Polaris TSA Playbook (v4.2, Jan. 15, 2025); Andersen instructions (Apr. 29, 2025)
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Privilege.** This memorandum is attorney-client privileged and attorney work product. It is intended solely for Polaris and its authorized counsel and should not be circulated outside the privilege group.

# Executive recommendation

**Do not circulate the Draft TSA without the attached seller-side markup.** The Draft is not conforming to the executed APA and, in its present form, creates material seller exposure. The most urgent items are: (i) the APA conflicts in the service standard, term/renewal, termination notice, fee mechanics, and liability cap; (ii) the unilateral consequential-damages waiver; (iii) the perpetual Polaris IP license; and (iv) the omission of operative IMMEX and LFPDPPP provisions for Monterrey.

**The liability and fee delta is quantifiable.** The Draft fee schedule charges 15% on IT rather than the APA ceiling of 10%, producing Draft monthly fees of \$1,139,000 rather than \$1,122,000. If services run for 18 months, the Draft 200%-of-total-fees cap could reach \$41,004,000, versus an APA-compliant trailing-12-month cap of approximately \$13,464,000 after month 12---a \$27,540,000 delta. At month 12, the analogous delta is approximately \$13,872,000.

**Board-level IP and Mexico risk.** Section 7.1 is a non-starter: it grants Trident a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to Polaris tools, methodologies, software, and know-how, including derivative-work and sublicensing rights. The Draft also addresses only U.S. data privacy, while the APA specifically requires Mexico provisions. The markup adds controller/processor allocation, privacy notices/consents, cross-border-transfer safeguards, incident response, and IMMEX responsibility/notice mechanics.

# Priority summary

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
         **Tier**         **Count / treatment**   **Core items**
  ----------------------- ----------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
         Critical         10 must-change items    APA service standard; term/renewal; 90-day termination notice; fee cap/mechanics; liability cap; mutual damages waiver; IP license; Mexico IMMEX/LFPDPPP; indemnity scope/cap; FTE/key-personnel conflict.

        Significant       11 target positions     Termination assistance; change orders; payment terms; escalation; audits; insurance; force majeure trigger; PA law/AAA Pittsburgh; non-solicit; termination for cause; schedule scope creep.

           Minor          4 cleanup items         Data ownership; renewal definitions; operational exclusions/dependencies; audit adjustment mechanics.
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Critical --- direct APA conflicts and must-change positions

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
     **Ref.**    **Issue / Draft**                             **Draft risk**                                                                                            **Markup position**                                                                                                                                                                                            **Position / basis**
  -------------- --------------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
       C-1       Service standard --- §3.1                     24-month lookback; "equal to or better than"; industry best practices.                                    12-month lookback; "substantially consistent"; no external best-practices standard or prioritization obligation.                                                                                               Firm. APA §§7.12(a), (f).

       C-2       Term / renewal --- §5.2                       Automatic 6-month renewals, up to 30 months, unless Polaris gives 120-day notice.                         18-month hard stop; no automatic renewal; only mutual written individual-service extension up to six months beyond the maximum, with extension pricing.                                                        Firm on no automatic renewal and mutual writing. APA §7.12(a).

       C-3       Individual-service termination --- §5.3       120-day notice.                                                                                           Exactly 90 days; it is both minimum and maximum.                                                                                                                                                               Firm. APA §7.12(c).

       C-4       Fees --- §6.1/§6.4/Schedule G                 IT at 15%; fixed/no-adjustment fees; out-of-pocket costs excluded from chargeable FLC.                    Uniform ≤10%; actual FLC adjustment mechanics and 5% estimate-consent rule; permit reasonable FLC out-of-pocket costs.                                                                                         Firm as to APA mechanics. APA §7.12(b).

       C-5       Liability cap --- §10.1                       200% of total fees paid as of claim.                                                                      Trailing 12 months; first-year fees paid since Closing; APA carve-outs.                                                                                                                                        Firm. APA §7.12(d).

       C-6       Consequential damages --- §10.2               Only Polaris waives; Trident is protected.                                                                Mutual waiver with third-party indemnity and APA-aligned carve-outs.                                                                                                                                           Firm; playbook identifies non-mutual waiver as unacceptable.

       C-7       IP license --- §7.1                           Perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license with modification/derivative/sublicense rights.   No license; access/use only to receive Services during the Term; separate license only if independently negotiated.                                                                                            Firm / board-level IP protection.

       C-8       Mexico cross-border --- §8.4; Schedules C/E   U.S.-only privacy clause; no IMMEX allocation or LFPDPPP processing terms.                                LFPDPPP-compliant controller/processor terms, notices/consents, cross-border safeguards, security/breach response; Trident primary IMMEX responsibility plus defined Polaris assistance and jeopardy notice.   Firm as to inclusion; local counsel to confirm technical wording. APA §7.12(g).

       C-9       Indemnities --- §§9.1--9.2                    Broad all-Loss indemnity, including direct breach and any legal violation; no cap alignment.              Third-party claims only; Trident use/reliance indemnity; Polaris gross negligence/fraud/willful misconduct threshold; APA cap structure.                                                                       Firm on scope/cap alignment.

       C-10      Staffing --- §§2.1/4.3/Schedule H             FTE minimums and buyer consent to reassign/replace Key Personnel.                                         FTE estimates; Polaris sole staffing discretion; notice and qualified replacement only.                                                                                                                        Firm on no consent; 15-business-day notice is negotiable. Exhibit H General Notes.
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

           Human Resources           \$137,500 / month     \$137,500 / month     ---

  ---------------------------------- ------------------------------------ ----------------------------------- -----------------

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

lines.text: > **Draft:** The Draft defines Renewal Term and Term as Initial Term plus Renewal Terms and makes the renewal concept operative in Schedule G.
> **DELETE** ~~"Renewal Term" \... each successive six (6)-month period \... "Term" means the Initial Term plus any Renewal Terms~~

> **ADD** [Delete "Renewal Term." "Term" means the Initial Term, together with any individual-service extension documented under §5.1 and APA §7.12(a). Update all references to "Renewal Term" and fixed fees during Renewal Terms to conform to the no-automatic-renewal structure.]{.underline}
| **Comment M-2 --- Minor --- Firm as conforming cleanup**                                                                                          |
| **Basis:** The definitions perpetuate the APA-conflicting automatic renewal structure even if §5.2 is deleted.                                    |
| **Risk:** Residual defined terms can be used to argue that a renewal remains available or that fixed fees survive an extension without repricing. |
## M-3 \| MINOR \| §2.2, §3.3, Schedule assumptions / Playbook §§2.2, 4.4 --- Operational exclusions and dependencies

> **Draft:** The Draft has helpful scope limitations and cooperation language but omits express exclusions for legal/tax/strategic advice, third-party contract breaches, and changes made to Polaris-wide systems, and does not clearly tie volume changes to change-order pricing.
> **DELETE** ~~Service Provider shall not be obligated to \... \[limited exclusions\]~~

> **ADD** [Service Provider is not required to provide services that would violate law, breach a third-party agreement, require new personnel/resources or technology solely for Trident, or constitute legal, tax, financial, or strategic advice. Polaris may modify delivery consistent with changes made for its own businesses. Material volume or scope increases require a signed change order.]{.underline}
| **Comment M-3 --- Minor --- Negotiable wording; risk allocation is important**                                                     |
| **Basis:** These are standard playbook exclusions and track APA §7.12(e)(i)--(iv).                                                 |
| **Risk:** The current drafting may turn reasonable operational changes or third-party licensing constraints into service breaches. |
## M-4 \| MINOR \| §14.2 / Playbook §9 --- Audit adjustment mechanics
> **Draft:** The Draft requires repayment of any overcharge with interest but does not provide a reciprocal payment for undercharges or a 5% threshold.
> **DELETE** ~~If an audit \... reveals that Service Provider has overcharged \... credit the amount \... together with interest~~

> **ADD** [If an audit identifies an overcharge exceeding five percent (5%) for the audited period, Polaris shall credit the overcharge and reasonable audit costs. If an audit identifies an undercharge, Trident shall pay the undercharge within thirty (30) days. No interest applies unless the audited party fails to pay a determined amount when due.]{.underline}
| **Comment M-4 --- Minor --- Negotiable cleanup**                                                                            |
| **Basis:** The playbook uses a 5% overcharge threshold and reciprocal undercharge payment.                                  |
| **Risk:** One-way audit adjustments create a unilateral penalty and incentivize audit claims even for immaterial variances. |
# Conforming provisions / no substantive seller change requested
Subject to the changes above, Polaris does not propose substantive changes to the following Draft TSA provisions, except for cross-references and renumbering caused by the markup:
> **•** §4.1 Steering Committee and §4.2 Service Managers (provided the committee cannot amend the TSA and does not control staffing).
> **•** §4.4 Monthly Reports, subject to removing open-ended requests and limiting reporting to information reasonably available without disproportionate burden.
> **•** §6.2 monthly invoicing cadence; §6.5 Transaction Taxes; and §6.6 disputed amounts, subject to revised Net 30 terms.
> **•** §8.1 confidentiality, §8.2 exceptions, and §8.3 three-year survival, subject to the enhanced Mexico data terms.

> **•** §11.3 disclaimer, §12.1 force-majeure notice/mitigation, §13.2 Polaris insurance, §15.3 notices, §15.4 assignment, §15.6 amendment/waiver, §15.7 severability, §15.8 counterparts, §15.9 no third-party beneficiaries, §15.10 independent-contractor relationship, and §15.11 interpretation.
